title: ColdVector account approach — outbound draft & pilot notes
content:
Quick brain-dump for ColdVector

Context + why ColdVector matters
- ColdVector: mid-market e-comm logistics platform (warehouse orchestration + edge routing for last-mile). Rapid growth in EU + US. Heavy real-time inference needs for routing decisions + ETA messaging.
- Why us: they care about predictable latency, multi-region failover, and cost. Likely sensitive to vendor lock / data residency (large EU footprint). Could be a fit for Redwood Dedicated or Private depending on security asks.

Stakeholders (mapped from LinkedIn + ACV notes)
- VP Eng / Head of Platform: Anita R. (primary technical DM) — cares about SLOs and operational simplicity.
- Head of ML / ML Infra: Tomas V. — wants low-latency, low-variance inference with GPU cost visibility.
- Head of BD/Partnerships: Claire M. — cares about integration speed & deployment model compatibility for partners.
- Procurement / Security: likely to ask for SOC2, data flow, KMS options.

Tech signals
- Tech stack: Kubernetes + GKE + Kafka + Redis (from job postings & infra repo hints).
- On-prem footprint: small cluster in EU region for compliance customers.
- Currently running a mix of quantized open models (they mentioned fuzzier models in a webinar) — suggests appetite for custom model ops and cost optimization.

Topline outbound hypothesis
- Position Redwood as: "Predictable, cost-efficient LLM inference that plugs into your platform with a path to private deployment and SLO guarantees."
- Initial ask: 15–30 minute technical sync with VP Eng or ML Infra.
- Anchor offer: 6-week pilot with a clear success metric (p50 latency < 120ms for routing model, 40% token cost reduction vs their baseline after batching/quant settings).

3-touch outbound cadence (sequence draft)
1) Short email (day 0) — subject: "Reduce inference cost & stabilize routing latency at ColdVector"
   - Opening 1 sentence: reference a concrete trigger (e.g., recent EU expansion/press release).
   - Value points (bulleted): latency + cost + private deployment option.
   - CTA: 15-min sync to share a tailored cost/latency sketch.
2) LinkedIn note (day 3) — informal: 1–2 lines, mention email + a one-page pilot outline attached (or link to Confluence).
3) Follow-up (day 7) — longer email with proposed pilot milestones + success metrics + a customer reference (anonymized).
4) If no response -> Ops-level reach (SRE/ML Infra) with a short technical note on KV cache + batching improvements we typically implement.

Sample first email (raw)
---
Subject: Reduce inference cost & stabilize routing latency at ColdVector
Hi Anita — congrats on the EU rollout this quarter. I work with platform teams at high-growth logistics companies to reduce inference cost while making latency more predictable.

We helped a similar customer drop per-request token cost by ~35% and reduce p95 latency variance by tuning batching + prefix caching and moving non-sensitive workloads to a shared hosted variant.

If this is relevant, I can share a short sketch of a 6-week pilot that targets p50 <120ms on your routing model and a clear cost baseline. 15 minutes next week?

— Maya
---

Objection handling (cheat-sheet)
- "We can't send production data to hosted vendors": explain Dedicated + Private options, KMS/HSM support, and network isolation (VPC peering). Offer on-site eval or bring-your-own-key.
- "Switching cost / integration time": propose a sidecar proxy approach for non-invasive traffic mirroring -> can run pilot with shadow traffic for 3 weeks. Emphasize SDKs + low-touch API.
- "Latency worries for routing decisions": highlight synchronous inference SLO examples, kernel selection and GPU placement strategies, and propose a short latency profiling exercise (we send a small harness).
- "Pricing will be higher than our infra": frame pricing vs effective per-inference unit cost after batching + caching; include Dedicated commit options and a rollback/fallback plan to their current cluster.

Pilot plan (6-week, high level)
- Week 0: Kickoff, access, and telemetry integration (tracing token counts, request size distribution).
- Week 1–2: Baseline profiling (p50/p95, token usage, cost estimate).
- Week 3–4: Implement batching + prefix caching + candidate quantization; run A/B against baseline (canary).
- Week 5: Stabilize, run scale test with shadow traffic at 2x expected load.
- Week 6: Review success metrics, propose rollout (Dedicated reserve or Private deployment).

Success criteria (proposed)
- p50 latency on routing model improved to <120ms OR p95 variance reduced by 60%
- Unit token cost reduction >=30% with preserved model accuracy (±2% business metric on ETA precision)
- Clear ops runbook for failover to hosted variants in region outages

Pricing anchor thoughts (notes to self)
- Offer two pilot flavors: "hosted quick-start" (lowest friction, limited EU residency guarantee) vs "private pilot" (VPC, KMS, longer setup).
- Anchors: show per-token baseline vs projected per-token after optimizations; mention Dedicated monthly commit as an option if predictable throughput is needed.

Open questions / things to confirm before outreach
- Exact model size and typical sequence length for routing inference (need from ML infra).
- Does ColdVector have strict data residency for routing telemetry? EU-only?
- Who owns procurement timeline and what approvals are needed for pilot (legal/security contact)?

Next tactical steps (todo list)
- [ ] Pull last quarter press + funding note to reference in email (Priya)
- [ ] Build quick latency/cost sketch using assumed numbers (Liam)
- [ ] Draft pilot one-pager for Confluence (link in linked_artifacts) and attach to cadence messages (Glenira)
- [ ] Run a short smoke script to generate example latency graphs for VP Eng slide (me)

Notes to self: keep outreach snappy and technical. Avoid generic AI marketing language — call out specific infra problems (KV cache, batching, kernel selection) that resonate with platform teams. Use the pilot as a low-risk evaluation with clear telemetry and rollback.

Thread history/refs (quick)
- Mentioned ColdVector at logistics summit (Dec 2025) — saved slide deck -> attach to Confluence page.
- Security checklist: SOC2 + ISO? check with Security team before private-pilot conversation.

End of scratchpad.

Rough export of candidate subject lines for A/B testing:
- "Cut inference cost for routing by 30% — quick sketch inside"
- "How ColdVector can stabilize routing latency across EU + US"
- "Pilot: 6 weeks to a predictable routing inference stack"
